notable_absence.finding: The RBAC section lists cloud-PROVIDER permissions required to operate cbbackupmgr against remote storage (AWS actions like GetObject/PutObject; Azure's 'Storage Blob Data Owner'; GCP's 'Storage Object Admin') alongside an explicit caveat that these 'are subject to change between releases' - but never once cross-references the Couchbase-side RBAC roles (data_backup, analytics_admin, eventing_admin, fts_admin) documented on cbbackupmgr-generate.md that are ALSO required for the same operation against the same cluster. A cloud backup needs both a cloud-provider IAM grant and a Couchbase Server role, and no single page states that a user needs both at once. The cloud-provider roles themselves are deliberately not minted as Couchbase concepts here - they belong to AWS/Azure/GCP's own IAM systems, a foreign domain this ontology does not own, matching the precedent set by relational:table.

cross_component_finding: cbbackupmgr-cloud.md's AWS/Azure/GCP are a genuine name collision with the already-promoted cloud-provider:aws/azure/gcp family, and NOT a case for reuse: the promoted concepts are explicitly typed as 'a Capella deployment substrate' - i.e. what infrastructure a CAPELLA CLUSTER runs on - while this page's AWS/Azure/GCP are external object-storage TARGETS a Server-side CLI archives to. Nothing connects a Capella cluster's hosting provider to a cbbackupmgr archive's storage provider; they happen to share three brand names because there are only three major clouds; that is a coincidence of the market, not a documented relationship. Filed under a fresh object-store: namespace rather than reusing cloud-provider: to avoid silently asserting the two things are the same axis.
cross_product_finding: None of this page's cloud-object-storage content bears on Capella - Capella's own snapshot/backup facility (cloud/clusters/cloud-snapshots.md, per the registry's service:backup-service collision note) is a wholly separate, provider-managed mechanism from cbbackupmgr writing an archive INTO a customer-controlled S3/Blob/GCS bucket. The two 'backup + cloud' stories in this corpus (cbbackupmgr writing archives to object storage vs. a CSP's own snapshot service backing up a Capella cluster) remain unrelated and unmerged, consistent with the module's no-twin framing.
